scope.summary: This Indian Standard specifies the material properties, plies, dimensional tolerances, galvanizing parameters, and testing protocols for stranded galvanized steel wire strands used primarily for fencing, agricultural enclosures, and security barriers.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or attach the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' on wire bundles or packaging coils to demonstrate conformity.

requirements.detail: Fencing strand is fabricated by twisting individual wires together, primarily in 3-ply (3-wire) or 7-ply (7-wire) configurations (comprising one core wire and six outer helical wires).
Standard individual wire nominal diameters range from 1.6 mm to 4.0 mm. A highly standard railway-grade and commercial specification uses a nominal single wire diameter of 1.6 mm.
Base steel must be drawn from low-carbon steel wire rods to facilitate cold drawing and tight helical twisting without physical joint failure or wire fracture.
Individual wires must undergo a hot-dip galvanizing process prior to stranding, conforming strictly to the medium or heavy coating requirements of IS 4826.
Wires must withstand wrapping around a mandrel of equal diameter for 8 complete turns without cracking, splitting, or showing zinc coating flaking.

Coating uniformity is verified using copper sulphate dip tests (conforming to IS 2633), requiring the wire to survive a minimum number of 1-minute dips without depositing bright, adherent metallic copper.

requirements.requirement_type: Uniform Lay Length and Ordinary Lay Direction
requirements.detail: The lay length (pitch of helical turns) must be uniform to ensure balanced tension, using a standard right-hand ordinary lay unless otherwise agreed.
Observed or calculated dimensions, lay lengths, coating weights, and tensile strengths must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 to determine code compliance.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2140 : 1978 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing construction, dimensional, material, and testing requirements for stranded galvanized steel wire used in fencing. Developed under Sectional Committee MED 10, the code unifies fencing strand configurations in India. It defines standardized 3-ply and 7-ply constructions using individual wires ranging from 1.6 mm to 4.0 mm, enforces strict hot-dip galvanizing weights and uniformity checks (via wrapping tests and copper sulphate dips), and integrates directly with companion fencing standards (IS 278 and IS 2721) to form highly secure, high-durability perimeter barriers.
